items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; the program rebuilds the context each call and includes earlier results. Option a shows the belief that the model remembers by itself.
A new session starts with an empty context, so facts must be saved outside it and loaded back. Option a treats this as a size problem; it is a persistence problem.

items.answer: Retrieval sends only the few relevant pages, so each call costs far fewer tokens and recall is better than with a huge context.
accepted: recall gets worse with long context
you pay for every token on every call
items.rationale: Any one valid reason is enough: cost (every token is paid for on every call), context rot (recall degrades as context grows), or that manuals can grow past the window. Saying a big window removes the need for retrieval is wrong.
The system prompt is part of the context of every call: 2,000 tokens x 5 calls = 10,000. An answer of 2,000 treats it as sent once.
Notes written outside the context survive a reset and can be read back; the model itself keeps nothing between calls.
